_label: SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA. The Hartwell family, Alder Creek and every person, place and event below are invented for demonstration. Any resemblance to real people is coincidental.

memories.title: Grandma Rosa's Sunday cinnamon bread
memories.body:
Every Sunday after church Grandma Rosa filled the kitchen at Maple Lane with the smell of cinnamon bread. She never wrote the recipe down. Lily, then eight, stood on a wooden stool and learned to knead the dough by pressing it with the heel of her hand until it stopped sticking.

The secret, Rosa said, was a spoonful of honey in the warm milk and letting the dough rise beside the stove for exactly as long as it took to finish the crossword. Lily still makes it every autumn.

memories.title: The summer the river flooded
memories.body:
In July 1983 the Alder Creek rose over its banks after three days of rain. Tomas, who was eleven, carried his little sister Lily on his shoulders through knee-deep water to the neighbour's barn. They spent the night on hay bales listening to the rain on the tin roof while the grown-ups moved the furniture upstairs.

The next morning the whole street cleaned mud from the porches together. Tomas says it was the most frightened and the happiest he has ever been.

memories.title: Grandpa Elias and the railway yard
memories.body: Elias Hartwell began work at the Alder Creek railway yard in 1955 as a boiler cleaner at just sixteen. Within ten years he was repairing steam locomotives, and later diesel engines. He carried a brass pocket watch that the stationmaster gave him on his first payday, and he was never late for a shift in thirty-four years.

memories.title: How Elias met Rosa
memories.body: Rosa and Elias met at the spring dance in the town hall in May 1960. Elias had a borrowed jacket two sizes too big, and Rosa laughed at it before she agreed to dance. They married eighteen months later in the small stone chapel on Maple Lane, and Rosa wore her mother's lace veil.

memories.title: Letter from Aunt Marisol, 1991
memories.body: Dear Rosa, the orange trees are blooming again and the whole courtyard smells of blossom. I wish you could see them. Papa's old guitar is still in the hall and Mateo plays it badly every evening. Tell the children that the house in Valencia is waiting for them any summer they like. Write soon. Your sister, Marisol.

memories.title: La receta de la abuela: arroz con leche
memories.body: Mi tía Marisol preparaba arroz con leche cada Nochebuena. Hervía la leche con una rama de canela y la cáscara de un limón, y removía despacio durante casi una hora. Decía que el secreto era tener paciencia y no dejar nunca de remover.

memories.title: Moving to Alder Creek
memories.body: In September 1954 the Hartwell family left the coast and travelled four hours by train to Alder Creek, where Elias's father had found work. Elias's mother Ida carried a single trunk with the good plates wrapped in newspaper. The first night they slept on the floor of the empty house on Maple Lane and ate bread and cheese by candlelight.

memories.title: Tomas builds the treehouse
memories.body: In the summer of 1982 Grandpa Elias helped Tomas build a treehouse in the old oak behind the house. Elias insisted on measuring everything twice and taught Tomas to use a spirit level. The treehouse had a rope ladder, a trapdoor and a tin sign that read 'Captain's Deck'. Lily was allowed up only if she knew the password.

memories.title: Lily's wedding day
memories.body: Lily married Daniel Okafor on 21 August 2004 in the garden at Maple Lane. Tomas gave a speech that made everyone cry, and Daniel's mother taught the Hartwells a dance that lasted until midnight. Lily wore Rosa's lace veil, forty-four years after Rosa wore it, and the cinnamon bread was served at the reception.

memories.title: The winter Grandpa Elias retired
memories.body: Elias worked his last shift at the railway yard on 15 December 1989. His colleagues gave him a framed photograph of the first locomotive he ever repaired. Rosa met him at the gate with a thermos of hot cocoa, and they walked home through the snow without saying much.

memories.title: Rosa's advice about kindness
memories.body: When Tomas was nineteen and worried about his future, Rosa told him: 'Be kind first, clever second. People forget what you knew, but they remember how you made them feel.' He wrote it on a card and still keeps it in his wallet.

memories.title: The night the lights went out on Maple Lane
memories.body: During the great ice storm of February 1987 the power was off for four days. Rosa lit candles in every window and told the children stories at the kitchen table about the old house, including one about a lantern that seemed to move by itself in the hallway. Lily was convinced she heard footsteps upstairs; it was only the ice cracking the gutters.

memories.title: Daniel's first visit to Maple Lane
memories.body: Daniel came to Maple Lane for the first time in November 2001, so nervous that he brought three bunches of flowers. Rosa put him to work peeling potatoes and decided within an hour that he would do. He still says the cinnamon bread was the best thing he had ever eaten.

memories.title: विरासत की दिवाली
memories.body: हर साल दिवाली पर पूरा परिवार आँगन में दीये जलाता था। मारिसोल मौसी रंगोली बनाती थीं और बच्चे मिठाई बाँटते थे। यह परंपरा आज भी हमारे घर में जारी है।

transcripts.title: Tomas remembers the flood (synthetic transcript, no audio)
transcripts.text: I remember the water was cold and brown and it came right up to my belt. I held Lily's legs so she would not fall. The barn smelled of hay and rain.
